classification.difficultyReason: Identify the hypotenuse, apply Pythagoras with surd givens and simplify exact lengths.

content.prompt: Determine the unknown side of the following right-angled triangles.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with a horizontal lower leg, vertical right leg and rising hypotenuse. The right-angle marker is at the lower-right vertex.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular legs have lengths 4 and 2√2; the hypotenuse is unknown.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied leg lengths and right-angle marker are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the unknown side. By Pythagoras,
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=4^2+(2\sqrt{2})^2\\x^2&=16+8\\x^2&=24\\x&=2\sqrt{6}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with a vertical left leg, horizontal upper leg and hypotenuse rising from lower left to upper right. The right-angle marker is at the upper-left vertex.
spec.mathematics: The vertical leg is 2√6 and the hypotenuse is 3√6; the horizontal leg is unknown.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied vertical-leg and hypotenuse lengths and right-angle marker are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the unknown side. By Pythagoras,
$$\begin{align*}x^2+(2\sqrt{6})^2&=(3\sqrt{6})^2\\x^2+24&=54\\x^2&=30\\x&=\sqrt{30}.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unshaded inverted triangle with a horizontal upper hypotenuse and two descending legs meeting at a lower right-angle vertex.
spec.mathematics: The hypotenuse is 8 and the left sloping leg is 2√7; the right sloping leg is unknown.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied hypotenuse and left-leg lengths and right-angle marker are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the unknown side. By Pythagoras,
$$\begin{align*}x^2+(2\sqrt{7})^2&=8^2\\x^2+28&=64\\x^2&=36\\x&=6.\end{align*}$$
